What's new in Vekrun 0.4.6 — Runs that fix their own setup

• A Factory run no longer stops because Lima, the tool that gives each Work Item its own VM, is missing: the run installs it (one time — Lima's official build, checked against its published checksum, no administrator rights) and carries on. The top bar no longer says an agent is ready for Factory runs while Lima is missing, and Factory readiness has an Install Lima button.
• Fixed: a project with git hooks (husky, pre-commit) could lose a finished task with "npm: not found". Vekrun's own snapshot of the work in the VM no longer runs the project's hooks; your tests, run on a fresh VM, are what prove the work.
• Python projects get a Python their packages have prebuilt wheels for: unless the project pins one exactly, Vekrun takes the newest settled Python line rather than the one that just shipped, and says why in the environment notes.
• When a run stops, the reason is in plain words. Stack traces and tool output stay one click away (Show the full error) and in Run output.
